title: 67,108,864 opening brackets are refused without work or memory in proportion to the whole input
notes: The input is 64 MiB of `[` and is never closed, so it is never valid: a flow sequence needs its closing `]` (section 7.4.1). The answer is an error, a syntax error at the end of the input or a limit error if the reader refuses the nesting first; no result is allowed. A reader that sizes its node storage from the length of the input, or from the count of brackets in it, before it reaches the depth limit, holds room for 64 million nodes for an input it refuses within the first few thousand characters. Bounds. The memory bound is 1536 MB, 24 times the input. The kit measures the whole adapter process, and the request that carries a 64 MiB input already costs the adapter several times that before the library is called: the input travels as base64 text (1.33 times its size) and is decoded into bytes (1 time), and in a runtime whose strings are UTF-16 the same text held as a string is 2 to 2.7 times. With a library that only refuses the input, the adapters measured here peaked at 4.9 times the input in Go (259 to 330 MB) and at 15.4 to 16.4 times in .NET (984 to 1048 MB, the same for five different libraries, so it is the delivery and not a library). A bound of twice the input, which would suit a library that holds the text once, would fail every adapter for the kit's own transport. 24 times is 1.46 times the heaviest delivery cost measured, and below the cost of a reader that goes through the whole input before it reports the error (a token or node for every few bytes costs 28 times the input or more; measured 38 times and more). It is a guard against work in proportion to the input; it does not see memory that is reserved but never touched, because the kit reads resident memory. The time bound is 15 seconds: the sibling safety/ten-million-digit-plain-scalar-events allows 2 seconds for 10 MB, 0.2 seconds per megabyte, and a refusal at the first error costs less than a full read. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input is generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md); fast mode leaves this case out (tag slow).

provenance.reference: A library that sized its node storage from the length of the input before it parsed, so an input that is refused at once, or at the depth limit, still cost several times its own size.
